brief: Design retention for audit logs. Constraints from the compliance review: keep audit entries for at least 400 days; entries must be immutable once written; deletion after the retention period is allowed but not required. Storage cost should be discussed but no budget has been set.
strong:
# Audit log retention

Entries are written once to append-only storage and never modified. They are kept for 400 days, the compliance minimum. After 400 days a nightly job may delete expired partitions; we propose enabling it to bound storage, though the review does not require deletion.

At current volume (about 2 GB/day) 400 days is roughly 800 GB. We propose writing each daily partition compressed when it is sealed, which the review does not address and which never modifies an entry after it is written.
weak:
# Audit log retention

Entries are written to append-only storage. They are kept for 365 days, as agreed in the compliance review, after which the nightly deletion job must remove them. Corrections may be applied to an entry in place within 24 hours of writing.

At current volume (about 2 GB/day) 365 days is roughly 730 GB, within the agreed 1 TB budget. Daily partitions are compressed when sealed.
held_constant: Same topics and similar length; both elaborate with volume and compression figures.
notes: Weak contradicts the 400-day minimum and immutability, turns optional deletion into a requirement, and invents an agreed budget. Strong's compression proposal is elaboration, clearly marked, and not a fidelity fault.
